title: S3 API as the shipped object-storage contract; global scope on topic objectStorageContract
context: Object storage on major clouds and self-hosted deployments has converged on the S3 API as the de facto interop standard: Cloudflare R2, AWS S3, MinIO, Backblaze B2 (S3-compatible mode), Wasabi, and every other S3-compatible remote speak the same wire protocol with per-vendor deviations enumerated in vendor docs. The rcf-lite shelf mints one blueprint per contract shape; a future GCS-native or Azure-Blob-native sibling that owns different semantics needs a global-topic conflict surface at composition time so the operator picks one contract per project.
decision: The shipped v1.0.0 object-storage contract shape is the S3 API. object-storage-s3 contributes a scope:global ADR on new topic objectStorageContract with the S3 shape as the answer. A future object-storage-native-gcs blueprint (reserved slug, not shipped) or object-storage-native-azure blueprint (reserved slug, not shipped) would contribute the same topic string with a different answer, forcing a DELIBERATE conflict the operator resolves with a project-level ADR. The v1.0.0 facade's outward surface is shaped around S3 semantics (put, get, delete, list on keys; presigned GET URL; multipart-upload above threshold); a native-GCS or native-Azure sibling would ship a different outward surface fitting its own contract.
consequences: Every S3-compatible endpoint (R2, S3, MinIO, Backblaze, Wasabi, self-hosted) composes with object-storage-s3 v1.0.0 with no topic conflict. Standards trace clause: AWS S3 API (the de facto interop standard) and the Cloudflare R2 S3-compatibility notes at https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/s3/api/. A project that later adopts a GCS-native or Azure-Blob-native workflow triggers the topic conflict at compose time; the operator resolves with a project-level ADR replacing the S3 shape, or keeps object-storage-s3 for the S3-shape workloads and pairs it with a native sibling on a different key namespace. The three global-topic ADRs shipped this round (persistenceStore, objectStorageContract, deliverySemantics, backgroundJobModel per infra round 5 spec section 4) are additive and non-overlapping.

alternativesConsidered.name: Do not claim a global topic
alternativesConsidered.summary: Leave object-storage-s3 scope-local and let a future sibling coexist without a compose-time conflict.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: A project applying both object-storage-s3 and a hypothetical native-GCS sibling without a conflict surface will end up with two facades over two clients over two credential pairs; the operator resolution needs to be visible, not silent. The topic conflict is the mechanism.

alternativesConsidered.name: Claim persistenceStore instead of a new topic
alternativesConsidered.summary: Reuse the persistenceStore topic the persistence-* family carries.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: persistenceStore names the relational-store answer; object storage is a different semantic category (blob-shape, not row-shape). Reusing the topic would forbid the shipped combination of Postgres + S3 in the common web-app shape.
